fact_text: Heavy income tax on salaries pushes Pakistani IT staff to work as freelancers who escape that tax, which the analyst argues erodes the talent base of documented listed IT companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'From Music to Financial Freedom - Ali Aftab Saeed's Journey towards Financial Freedom' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Physical gold bought in Pakistan nominally carries 18% tax, but buyers commonly avoid it; because the purchase is undocumented the holding cannot be insured against theft or flood.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'From Music to Financial Freedom - Ali Aftab Saeed's Journey towards Financial Freedom' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst works from a long-run average PSX return of roughly 18% a year, and uses it as the base case against which individual stocks are judged.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Across the 36 years of PSX history the analyst charts, about 23 years were positive and 13 negative; the blend of the two produces the roughly 18% long-run average.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In years when the analyst's bull-market framework is switched on, PSX has averaged roughly 30-35%; in bear-market years the average is about minus 10%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's bear-market checklist is rising interest rates, a widening current account deficit, political instability, falling FX reserves and a market PE pushed up to 13-14, which together argue for shifting part of a portfolio into fixed income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Through a Roshan Digital Account an overseas Pakistani can open a bank and brokerage account remotely, hold shares in CDC custody and convert the proceeds back into foreign currency, normally within one to two days.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Hub Power is a holding structure spanning independent power projects, oil and gas exploration and the Mega Motors venture that assembles BYD vehicles, plus one or two smaller businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Hub Power owns 47.5% of China Power Hub Generation Company, the CPEC coal power project whose dividends resumed as power-sector circular debt improved.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Hub Power has approved a dividend policy of about PKR 5 per share each quarter, roughly PKR 20 a year, which the analyst treats as an 8-9% yield stock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On the analyst's best case of 25,000 BYD units a year at PKR 1m profit each and a 10x PE, the venture is worth about PKR 250bn, half of which accrues to Hub Power, adding only around 40% to a market cap already near PKR 300bn.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because Hub Power already owns several large established businesses, the analyst argues a new vehicle venture cannot repeat a small assembler's multi-fold re-rating even if the cars sell well.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To value a newly launched vehicle brand the analyst multiplies plausible annual units by profit per unit, applies a modest PE, takes the parent's ownership share and compares the result with the parent's existing market cap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani refinery upgrade projects run from roughly $500-600m each to about $1bn for the larger ones, a very large investment relative to the small market capitalisations of some listed refiners.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A levy imposed on furnace oil turned refining into a policy-disadvantaged sector, and its reversal alongside a cleared path for upgrades is what the analyst sees as the sector's turning point.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Attock Refinery runs on locally produced crude from the KPK fields, so it escapes the import premium that is built into the weekly ex-refinery petrol and diesel price formula.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates roughly 90% of Pakistan's local crude discoveries end up at Attock Refinery, so continuing OGDC and Mari discoveries could lift its utilisation from around 70% towards 90% over a few years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst regards Attock Refinery as best placed to benefit from the new refinery policy because it is cash rich, has a strong balance sheet, holds valuable land and enjoys the local-crude advantage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Attock group's earlier exit from Attock Cement gave minority holders a good exit price, and repeated talk of Saudi interest in the refinery keeps a similar transaction as a possible, though unconfirmed, future catalyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst defines a multibagger as a stock compounding 25-30% a year against the roughly 18% an average PSX company delivers, which over a decade requires real profit growth rather than sentiment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats return on invested capital of about 30% as the central multibagger screen and says establishing a business's true ROIC is 70-75% of the research work.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: High ROIC comes from selling for cash rather than extending customer credit, and from a plant that was not enormously expensive to build; a capital-heavy plant combined with customer credit makes high ROIC very hard.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sectors with large informal players are poor hunting grounds for multibaggers, because undocumented competitors evade sales and income tax and set prices that leave the documented player a much thinner return.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buying a genuine multibagger at too high a PE can leave the stock sideways for two or three years while the overvaluation corrects, which is what usually causes investors to sell in frustration.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lucky Cement's long multibagger run rested on being first to adopt Chinese cement plant technology and on building captive gas power plants when Pakistani gas was cheap, giving it a power cost advantage and funding rapid expansion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lucky Cement's growth now comes from its power projects and its automobile business as much as from cement, with mining a planned addition, so the analyst says its future depends on the ROIC of those new avenues.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop became a multibagger on cheap LTFF long-term loans, a low export income tax rate, rapid expansion and global scale in socks; continuing it now depends on the newer apparel and denim segments earning well.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Textile exporters used to be taxed at about 1% of export value and could borrow under the LTFF scheme; LTFF is no longer available on those terms and, although super tax on exporters was removed, a 29% income tax now applies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the government has already decided to phase down the corporate super tax gradually in order to attract foreign direct investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX spent the first half of 2025 broadly sideways, and then rallied strongly in the second half once the Pakistan-India conflict improved the country's geopolitical standing and a well-received budget removed uncertainty.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A Pakistani apartment yielding PKR 100,000 a month of rent is typically worth PKR 25-35m, a gross yield of only about 3.5-5%, which the analyst contrasts with a mix of dividend stocks and fixed income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Planning Retirement with less savings, Multibagger Stocks & Refinery sector - Your Investment Q&A' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC and PPL together produce more than half of all oil and gas produced inside Pakistan, and their combined market value is above $4.5bn.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's 1997, 2001 and 2012 petroleum policies set exactly what price a producer receives; prices are linked to global oil but oil carries windfall levies and gas is capped, so a field's policy vintage determines its earning power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani petroleum policies apply a 40-50% windfall levy to the portion of the crude price above roughly $50-60 a barrel, so at $85 international oil a local producer realises only about $70-75.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local gas prices are linked to international crude but capped by policy: the 2001 policy caps the wellhead price near $3 per mmbtu and the 2012 policy near $6.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With similar drilling cost and success rates, a gas field priced under the 2012 petroleum policy earns roughly double what the same field would under the 2001 policy, so an analyst must know which policy a company's major fields fall under.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On a realised crude price around $52-53 a barrel, a Pakistani producer pays 12.5% royalty and about $12 a barrel of operating cost, leaving roughly $30-35 pre-tax and $20-25 after tax, before exploration capital.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the 2001 policy a $3 gas price less 12.5% royalty and about $1 of operating cost leaves roughly $1.5 pre-tax and about $1 after tax per unit, against roughly $3 pre-tax and $2 after tax on $5-6 gas under the 2012 policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gas price caps exist because exploration in Pakistan is a high-return business: the state sets a price that still leaves investors an adequate return while keeping gas cheap for citizens, as low-cost producers such as Russia also do.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's annual gas bill is roughly PKR 2 trillion, about half local production and half imported LNG, while low tariffs and line losses mean only about PKR 1.5 trillion is actually collected; the roughly PKR 500bn gap becomes circular debt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Imported Qatari LNG has the first right to payment and cannot be defaulted on, so the whole of any gas-sector collection shortfall is pushed onto local gas producers rather than shared.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The fastest way to measure circular-debt flow at an E&P is to compare the profit after tax reported in a quarter or half year with the increase in trade debts over the same period; the gap is profit that never arrives as cash.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Underpayment destroys an E&P's economics because royalty, taxes and operating costs must all be paid in cash while the unpaid portion is exactly the after-tax profit needed to recover drilling capital, so reinvestment stops.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PPL's management told the analyst it preferred keeping an old field on the roughly $3 gas policy rather than qualifying it for a $5-6 price, because royalty and tax would double in cash while the extra revenue stayed unpaid, creating a cash loss.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC produces roughly 35,000 barrels of oil and about 700 mmcfd of gas a day, with Qadirpur, Uch, the Tal block and Nashpa as its main fields, and earns close to half its revenue from oil and half from gas.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PPL produces about 650 mmcfd of gas but only around 10,000 barrels of oil a day, with Sui, Kandhkot, the Tal block and Adhi as its main fields, making it far more gas-weighted than OGDC.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil flows to refineries and is sold at the pump so it is paid for in cash, while gas prices are administered and burdened with LNG costs and line losses; an E&P with a higher oil share therefore converts far more profit into cash.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF reviews historically forced electricity tariff increases because power circular debt reached PKR 1-2 trillion; now that gas circular debt has also passed PKR 2 trillion, each review requires gas price increases and control of that stock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the latest IMF programme, if expensive imported LNG is diverted to a sector at a lower price, the resulting deficit must be recovered in the next six-monthly local gas price revision.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because old gas fields are priced on caps and crude above roughly $50-60 is taxed by windfall levy, a 20% fall in the international oil price cuts a Pakistani E&P's revenue by only about 5-7%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues a lower oil price is not clearly negative for Pakistani E&Ps: at $50 crude earnings fall only about 10-12%, while a cheaper gas bill shrinks circular debt, lifts cash profits and can re-rate the PE.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan imports roughly $15-20bn of oil a year, so a higher price widens the current account deficit, lifts inflation and forces rate increases; a 3-4 point rate rise can pull the market PE from about 8x down to 6.5x.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Very old Pakistani fields eventually pay 27.5% royalty instead of 12.5%; so far this has applied only to PPL's Sui field, from 2019, and to the Mari field, both discovered in the 1950s and 1960s.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC and PPL each hold an 8.33% stake in Reko Diq bought years ago at a much stronger rupee, so the analyst calculates that a Saudi purchase at the prices quoted in the press would be a one-off gain of only about PKR 10-20 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC and PPL have each invested about $100m in Abu Dhabi's Block 6; even if a discovery tripled that to roughly $400m combined, it is under 10% of their combined $4.5bn market value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC's published plan is to raise oil production from about 35,000 to 50,000 barrels a day over five to seven years, which also helps a country that must import most of its oil.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst dismisses electric vehicles as a volume risk for Pakistani producers because about 70% of oil consumed in Pakistan is imported, so local production would still be absorbed; the real EV risk is a lower global price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fixed-volume LNG contracts combined with weak gas demand have forced curtailment of some local gas production to protect the pipeline network, a problem the government is trying to fix by negotiating flexibility into the LNG contracts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A PKR 1-2 trillion circular-debt settlement cannot come out of the budget, so the analyst expects a dividend-reinvestment design: the state funds the companies, they declare dividends, and most of the cash returns to the state.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government owns about 85% of OGDC and roughly 70-75% of PPL, and because their boards are state-appointed they cannot shut fields in protest at unpaid bills the way a private operator might.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Captive power plants pay the highest gas price and involve few line losses, so an IMF-driven cut in their gas allocation only avoids recreating circular debt if the volume is redirected to high-slab users rather than cheap slabs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Kya Aapko OGDC PPL main Invest karna Chahie? - OGDC PPL explained in full detail' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank's long-run ROE is driven by its deposit franchise, the share of deposits held in non-remunerative current accounts, and the loss rate on its loan book, since depositors must be repaid in full whatever the loans do.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A strong deposit franchise means customers come to the bank rather than managers chasing deposits, which makes it far easier to convert them to current accounts; that franchise is also what earns a bank a higher PE.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because current accounts pay close to nothing, a rise in interest rates widens the spread earned on them, and that gain broadly offsets the mark-to-market loss on government bonds bought at lower yields.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats banks as largely insulated from an oil shock itself; the channel that matters is macro mismanagement, such as subsidising fuel or letting the current account deficit run, which compresses sector PEs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Among the large banks the analyst rates Meezan's deposit franchise as the strongest, with NBP and Bank of Punjab also strong because government institutions keep large deposits with them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Meezan Bank's stated dividend policy is to maintain about PKR 7 per share per quarter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: MCB's dividend policy is maintained at roughly PKR 9 per share per quarter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL's dividend policy is maintained at around PKR 8 per share per quarter.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank of Punjab has shifted from annual to semi-annual dividend payments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The dominant cost of making urea in Pakistan is gas, which the government supplies to fertilizer plants at a fixed price; it also refuses bag price increases unless that gas cost rises, which keeps sector profits stable through crises.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's urea manufacturing capacity is roughly equal to its own demand, and the local urea price sits far below international levels, so the business runs largely independent of global commodity swings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New fertilizer capacity requires a government policy granting gas allocation, as the 2001 fertilizer policy did; with no such policy in force expansion stalls, which is why the companies pay out a high share of cash as dividends.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fertilizer demand tracks farm economics: a commodity price spike improves farm incomes, and when imported DAP becomes expensive farmers shift towards fixed-price local urea, lifting urea volumes as happened in 2023.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's three main urea plants take low-BTU gas directly from the Mari field, which would need heavy processing to be fit for the national pipeline, so their supply is secure unless the field itself fails.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Two Punjab fertilizer plants run on imported LNG, so if gas is short and the state shuts them for a few months the remaining Mari-fed plants gain sales certainty and a little extra pricing power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC produces a share of its output as DAP following its merger with FFBL, while Fatima Fertilizer makes a share as NP.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NP and DAP prices rise in an oil shock while the gas cost of making them locally stays fixed, so producers of those grades such as Fatima Fertilizer and FFC see profits improve rather than suffer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst doubts urea exports will be allowed: local demand barely absorbs output, a 1-2m ton inventory is under two months of supply, and the government could tax exports so the gap between a PKR 5,000 local bag and PKR 12,000 abroad never reaches producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fertilizer sales are seasonal: roughly 40-45% falls in the first half of the calendar year and 55-60% in the second, with January-March weakest, so fixed cost absorption makes quarterly earnings and dividends look uneven.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: 2025 was a difficult year for Pakistani agriculture, with wheat falling to around PKR 2,000 early in the year, yet about 6.5m tons of urea were still sold over the year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC and Fatima Fertilizer have both invested in PIA, so how quickly the airline performs after privatisation accounts for an estimated 5-10% of their valuations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A refinery's margin is the average realised price of its product slate minus the crude price minus roughly $5 a barrel of chemicals and energy; when the product-crude differential widens from about $10 to $20 the per-barrel profit roughly triples.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Diesel normally trades about $30 a barrel above crude and is a refinery's highest-margin product, so the analyst watches that differential as the key swing factor in refining profits during a supply crisis.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Furnace oil is still roughly 25-35% of a Pakistani refinery's output and is the lowest, often negative, margin product; when a heavy levy makes it unsellable locally it must be exported at a loss, crushing overall refining profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the government argued in IMF talks that the furnace oil levy collects nothing because the fuel is simply exported, so reversing it in the budget would both restore refining profits and unlock upgrade investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Damage to Middle East refineries and LNG complexes takes anywhere from six months to five years to repair, so the analyst expects elevated refining margins to persist for six to twelve months rather than weeks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government prefers importing crude over refined product so that the refining margin is earned at home instead of being added to the current account deficit, which supports higher local refinery throughput.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To rank Pakistani refiners the analyst combines three disclosed numbers from company briefings: the share of output that is diesel, whether the refinery runs on local crude, and the share that is furnace oil.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When levies are placed on both furnace oil and gas, industrial users stop self-generating and shift their load to the national grid, which is what the furnace oil levy was designed to achieve.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank raises policy rates by much less than inflation rises when the inflation is cost-push and judged temporary, which limits the damage an oil shock does to equity valuations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst stresses that a stock can fall while the index doubles if the business trajectory turns negative, citing refineries lagging badly through a strong market until margins recovered.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Banking, Fertilizer Ya Refineries? Best Sector during Oil Crisis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 1990 Iraq-Kuwait war oil doubled from about $15 to $40 a barrel, and the supply hit of 5-6m barrels was roughly 10% of the 65m barrels a day the world then produced.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2022 Russia-Ukraine shock, sanctions affected roughly 7-9m barrels a day out of world consumption of about 100m, a disruption comparable in scale to the 1990 shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The decisive variable in stopping an oil shock from becoming a macroeconomic shock is passing the international price rise through to local petrol and diesel; that curbs consumption, protects the current account and switches on the automatic stabilisers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In each of the three big oil shocks the analyst studies, the equity market's low formed within roughly the first month of the event provided no fuel subsidy was given, and the following six months returned about 10-15%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Averaging the 1990 and 2022 oil shocks, investing six to seven months after the event returned roughly 50% over the next year and about 100% over two years, with the milder 2003 case better still.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil prices fall far more slowly than they rise: six months after the 1990 shock crude was still near $30, and after the 2022 shock it only slipped below $100 towards the end of that year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Above a certain price the international stabilisers engage: demand is destroyed, alternative routes open such as Iraqi trucking or Saudi exports via Suez, sanctions on other producers are relaxed, and US shale can bring wells on in six to nine months.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FX reserves are an economy's shock-absorbing capacity, which is why PSX can fall harder than Gulf markets during a Gulf conflict: thin reserves make investors fear devaluation, while larger reserves let the central bank hold rates steady.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government and local refineries agreed to cap the diesel margin over crude at $40 a barrel and then tightened it to $30, which held local diesel prices well below where an uncapped spread would have put them and limited inflation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When normal oil is $60-70 and the price has reached $100-120, the analyst argues 50-60% of the move is war premium already priced in, so fresh negative headlines are not a reason to assume further increases.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst allocates across three buckets: high-oil-price beneficiaries such as E&P and refineries, unaffected dividend sectors such as banks and fertilizer, and volatile cyclicals, holding at least 20% and at most 40% in each.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Within each portfolio bucket the analyst wants at least two sectors, and suggests inexperienced investors simply take the leading company in each sector rather than attempt company-level research.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats a forward market PE of around 8x as historically attractive for PSX and as evidence that the market carries no overvaluation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Index volatility decays sharply after the first six months of a conflict-driven shock, with daily swings narrowing from roughly 5,000 points to the 1,500-2,000 range as uncertainty is absorbed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst varies monthly contributions against the oil price, adding more when crude is above roughly $85-90 because the market is then in a corrective phase, and less when it falls back towards $75.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Oil Back Above $100: Should You Still Invest in PSX?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
